final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS merger framework with 100 billion CHF loss protection, SNB emergency liquidity, and AT1 preservation—announced Sunday 7 PM with a Friday night SNB statement to prevent weekend deposit flight. Critical legal ambiguity remains on whether AT1 preservation is standalone systemic stabilization or merger consideration.
minority_objections: AT1 representative repeatedly warned that preserving AT1 as a merger condition (rather than standalone systemic measure) exposes the government to litigation and Article 99 collapse
Wealth client objected that any hedging language ('subject to completion') would trigger immediate client flight Saturday morning
SNB warned that deposit backstop only buys 24-48 hours if outflows exceed 40 billion, requiring Parliamentary authorization the government doesn't have
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs AT1 rep: whether to sign a memo characterizing AT1 preservation as standalone systemic stabilization (Federal Council refused, citing timing and legal defensibility)
FINMA vs Federal Council: whether to announce 'immediately active' loss protection or 'subject to completion' (resolved by ministerial decree under Article 99)
UBS CEO vs Federal Council: whether 100 billion covers legacy assets only or also deposit flight (left ambiguous in final framework)
key_concessions: Federal Council committed to 100 billion loss protection as binding ministerial decree under Article 99, no Parliamentary gate
UBS signed AT1 preservation amendment at 11:47 PM after Federal Council ultimatum threatening to declare merger collapse
SNB agreed to issue Friday night public statement on emergency liquidity to prevent weekend deposit flight, despite undercutting Sunday announcement strategy
Federal Council accepted 'merger' framing (not 'acquisition') in Sunday announcement to preserve client confidence
red_lines: Federal Council: will not sign memo characterizing AT1 preservation as standalone systemic measure before merger closes
AT1 rep: will litigate if AT1 writedown occurs or if government cannot prove preservation was independent of merger consideration
UBS: will not proceed without signed AT1 preservation amendment by midnight
Wealth client: will move assets Saturday morning if Sunday announcement contains hedging language like 'subject to completion'
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Parliamentary ratification risk: multiple agents warned Article 99 defense collapses if Parliament discovers AT1 preservation was UBS merger condition, but Federal Council proceeded without securing legal cover
Deposit flight modeling: SNB's 40 billion threshold before needing Parliament was never validated against UBS or CS projections of actual weekend outflows
Litigation timing: AT1 rep warned clients would sue Monday regardless of Parliamentary outcome, but no legal strategy was developed to address immediate court challenges

UBS shareholder backlash: UBS CEO warned shareholders would argue they overpaid for a broken bank if loss protection framed as merger facilitation, but Federal Council's messaging strategy left this exposure unresolved
downstream_risk_variables: Whether deposit outflows in first 48 hours post-announcement exceed SNB's 40 billion Parliamentary threshold
Whether Parliament accepts 'systemic stabilization' justification when AT1 preservation was UBS merger condition
Whether AT1 creditors successfully challenge preservation as ultra vires government overreach
Whether UBS shareholders challenge merger terms as overpayment subsidized by public backstop
Whether Friday night SNB statement prevents Saturday deposit flight or merely delays it until Sunday announcement gaps become visible
uncertainty_notes: The 100 billion loss protection scope remains ambiguous (legacy assets vs deposit flight coverage). The legal foundation for AT1 preservation is contested—Federal Council claims Article 99 systemic authority, but refused to sign standalone memo, leaving exposure if Parliament or courts determine it was merger consideration. Deposit flight modeling was never reconciled between SNB's 40B threshold and actual projected outflows. The Friday night SNB statement may prevent weekend panic or may telegraph government desperation, depending on market interpretation.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: FINMA R1: 'Standalone survival is not credible—solvency doubts are real, and a pure funding run will trigger those doubts by Monday. We need to model a merger or assisted resolution.' This recognition drove the entire pivot to UBS acquisition path.
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Federal Council R1 proposed 100B loss backstop for UBS merger—became the binding framework. UBS signed AT1 amendment at 11:47 PM after ultimatum. Merger announcement locked for Sunday 7 PM.
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council committed 100B loss protection as ministerial decree under Article 99, SNB activated emergency liquidity Friday night. Government backstop was non-negotiable condition—UBS CEO R1: 'UBS won't move without certainty on loss protection.'
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client R2: 'I lose half my AUM by Monday' if announcement hedges. CS CEO R2: 'my clients still run Monday morning' without locked framework. Deposit flight drove Friday night SNB statement and Sunday announcement timing.
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 rep R1 raised writedown risk if UBS demands capital structure cleanup. Federal Council R2 set red line: 'not prepared to write down AT1 instruments without explicit legal cover.' UBS signed preservation amendment after ultimatum—became binding constraint.
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep R8-R9 repeatedly challenged whether preservation was standalone systemic measure or merger sweetener, warning Article 99 collapses if latter. Federal Council refused to sign standalone memo, leaving legal ambiguity that shaped final framework's vulnerability.
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned 'my clients will be in court by Monday' (R1) and 'my clients sue Monday regardless' (R9), but no concrete legal strategy was developed to address this—acknowledged as risk but did not force a decision change.
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Time pressure escalated from R1 (FINMA demands numbers 'within the hour') to R9 (midnight UBS countersignature deadline). Federal Council R6 ultimatum: sign by 11 PM or declare collapse. Compression forced AT1 amendment signature and Friday night SNB statement.
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Wealth client R2: 'I lose half my AUM by Monday.' CS CEO R5: clients 'move everything Monday morning' if framing wrong. Mentioned repeatedly as background threat but did not itself force a specific decision—the Sunday 7 PM timing was set to preempt it.
